subject: Stability thermometer — MAP rebasing & escalation
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Simon Gray <simon.gray@healthcorps.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@healthcorps.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Stability thermometer — MAP rebasing & escalation

Hi Simon —

Thanks again for the candid note yesterday. Per our call, I attached a condensed MAP v2 that aligns milestones to your security and procurement gates. Two quick things we observed that are driving close-date uncertainty: (1) SOC evidence delivery window still has a three-week variance from your side, and (2) the acceptance criteria for the pilot load test need a tighter definition so our infra team can size windows deterministically.

Can you confirm the earliest SOC evidence handoff you can commit to? If your procurement needs an internal review step, point me to the owner so I can loop them directly.

Attached: MAP_v2_HealthCorps.xlsx (row-level timeline), SOW_draft_v3.pdf (procurement-friendly redlines), acceptance_criteria.md (proposal).

Proposed short next steps:
- You confirm SOC evidence owner and earliest date
- We adjust MAP to a conservative/optimistic pair and flag the canaries
- If SOC slips >5 business days we trigger the contingency cadence (below)

Contingency cadence (proposal): weekly TPS + bi-weekly exec sync until stabilization; automatic fallback to Redwood-quantized model for pilot to keep latency deterministic.

Thanks,
Grace

--
Grace O'Connor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0142
From: Simon Gray <simon.gray@healthcorps.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@healthcorps.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Stability thermometer — MAP rebasing & escalation

Grace —

Appreciate the doc. Short answers: we can pull SOC evidence but earliest realistic handoff is 2027-05-17 (was hoping sooner). Procurement has a mandatory 5-business-day internal legal review once SOW is updated; owner is Marta Levin (marta.levin@healthcorps.com).

On acceptance criteria: can you turn acceptance_criteria.md into a checklist with pass/fail thresholds? That will make our PMO sign-off faster.

If we hit May 17 for SOC, what's the updated close window?

—Simon
Director of Product, HealthCorps
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Simon Gray <simon.gray@healthcorps.com>, Procurement Team <procure@healthcorps.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 13:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Stability thermometer — MAP rebasing & escalation

Simon — thanks, that's helpful.

If SOC handoff is 2027-05-17 and procurement legal needs 5 business days, conservative path pushes go-live acceptance out to 2027-06-02. Optimistic path (if we get partial SOC artifacts earlier and legal approves redlines concurrently) could keep go-live around 2027-05-24.

I'm looping Rishi to weigh in on technical gating (load-test thresholds and fallback cadence). Rishi — quick ask: can our infra deliver a quantized pilot image and a prefixed KV-cache snapshot so HealthCorps can run a deterministic 10k-message load test without infra variance? If yes, how long to stand up test harness once SOC artifacts are present?

Thanks,
Grace
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Simon Gray <simon.gray@healthcorps.com>, Procurement Team <procure@healthcorps.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Stability thermometer — MAP rebasing & escalation

All —

We can produce a quantized pilot image and a KV snapshot. Timeline: once SOC artifacts are ingested (we need evidence of encryption-at-rest config + network egress matrix), infra needs 3 business days to spin the harness and 2 business days to run deterministic load runs and produce the report. So end-to-end from SOC handoff: ~5 business days. That aligns with the optimistic path if legal runs in parallel, but pulls to conservative if legal waits for full SOC package.

I've attached a short tech checklist (acceptance_criteria.md updated) with measurable thresholds (p95 latency, token cost delta, deterministic output similarity) and a stub load schedule.

-J

--
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Stability thermometer — MAP rebasing & escalation (internal)

Team —

Quick internal triage before I escalate: HealthCorps pushed SOC to 5/17 which yields conservative go-live ~6/02; procurement owner is Marta Levin (procurement review 5 business days). Risks and asks below. Please annotate by EOD so I can include in the exec note.

Risks:
- SOC handoff slips further (healthcare vendor dependencies) — high
- Procurement legal flags SOW redlines (pricing/indemnity) — medium
- Load-test failure due to data profile mismatch — medium

Recommended mitigations:
1) Insert a canary acceptance with quantized model to validate latency and correctness on 5/24 (Rishi leads)
2) Offer a contract amendment that allows a 2-week soft-acceptance window with defined rollback conditions to reduce procurement resistance (Jonas to prepare emendation)
3) Ask HealthCorps for a partial SOC artifact drop (encryption keys config + egress matrix) by 5/10 to accelerate infra prep

Please add timing for mitigation items and owners.

-Grace
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Simon Gray <simon.gray@healthcorps.com>, Procurement Team <procure@healthcorps.com>
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Stability thermometer — MAP rebasing & escalation

Simon — thanks for the clarity. We reviewed internally and can take the two-track approach below to reduce overall close risk. Proposed items:

1) Canary / soft-acceptance plan (5/24): Redwood delivers quantized pilot image + KV snapshot; HealthCorps runs deterministic load (our infra supports and will certify results).
2) Contract amendment (single page emendation) to allow a 14-day soft-acceptance window and capped liability during the pilot. Draft attached: SOW_draft_v3.pdf (redlines).
3) Partial SOC pre-handoff request: if HealthCorps can drop encryption config and egress matrix by 5/10, we will start harness spin-up immediately and target the 5/24 canary.

If HealthCorps confirms partial drop by 5/10 and Marta runs legal in parallel, optimistic close remains 5/24–5/28. If not, conservative close target is 6/02 and we will schedule weekly exec syncs starting 5/12.

Simon — can you confirm Marta can review redlines in parallel and whether 5/10 partial SOC is feasible?

Best,
Jonas
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
